brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four bases at one level (piece:0,0,0, piece:0,-1,0, piece:1,-1,0, piece:-1,0,0;half-n), 22 parts in total including the caps and joint bolts. I added the fourth base so the spike and drawer don't clash.
drawer:0#-1,0#cut is on the cut face of the half base at (-1,0).

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,-1|0,0|1,-1 is a mount spike at the corner where the three full bases meet.
platform-sm is set on the mount spike.

finish.summary:
I built a compact desk unit from four bases with 22 parts: three full bases at (0,0), (0,-1) and (1,-1), plus a north half base at (-1,0). A drawer sits on the cut face of the half base. A mount spike with a small platform stands where the three full bases meet. Open faces are capped with end caps and the joints are bolted. check_build found no rule issues, and the mesh-collision check reads clear. 

My first plan was three bases with the spike at the half base's corner, but the configurator refused that spike (SPIKE_CLASH) because the drawer fills that corner. So I added the fourth base at (1,-1) to give the spike its own three-base corner. A solid spike can't carry a platform, so I used the mount type. I added no props because the brief didn't ask to show the unit in use.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
